 By  
 Ryan O'Rourke 
 Published Nov 14, 2026, 4:00 AM EST 
 Ryan O'Rourke is a Senior News Writer at Collider with a specific interest in all things adult animation, video game adaptations, and the work of Mike Flanagan . He is also an experienced baseball writer with over six years of articles between multiple outlets, most notably FanSided's CubbiesCrib . Whether it's taking in a baseball game, a new season of Futurama or Castlevania: Nocturne , or playing the latest From Software title, he is always finding ways to show his fandom. When it comes to gaming and anything that takes inspiration from it, he is deeply opinionated on what's going on. Outside of entertainment, he's a graduate of Eureka College with a Bachelor's in Communication where he honed his craft as a writer. Between The IV Leader at Illinois Valley Community College and The Pegasus at Eureka, he spent the majority of his college career publishing articles on everything from politics to campus happenings and, of course, entertainment for the student body. Those principles he learned covering the 2020 election, Palestine, and so much more are brought here to Collider, where he has gleefully written on everything from the SAG-AFTRA and WGA strikes to Nathan Lane baby-birding sewer boys.

 There is no shortage of procedural franchises ongoing across network television in 2026, but none have maintained their momentum quite as well for quite as long as NCIS . The flagship is in the middle of its 24th season, and a lot has already happened, between the return of Tony DiNozzo ( Michael Weatherly ) as the new director of the titular agency , the trial of McGee's ( Sean Murray ) son for hacking the NCIS database, and Torres ( Wilmer Valderrama ) facing his dark past , among other things. Meanwhile, CBS has also taken the formula to the Big Apple for the first time with the new spin-off NCIS: New York starring LL COOL J 's Sam Hanna and brought Mark Harmon back for one more dangerous mission in NCIS: Origins Season 3. Despite all the action, the agents are about to take their second leave of the month soon.

 Already, NCIS Tuesdays had to hit pause to accommodate Midterm election coverage to kick off November. Now, the franchise is taking off for the holidays. November 24 will see no new episodes from any of the three shows grace the small screen ahead of Thanksgiving, instead opting for re-airings. It's been typical for CBS to hold back episodes of the procedural crime drama franchise during this special occasion, even if they aren't airing on turkey day itself. The schedule will be back to normal on December 1, with only a few weeks left until midseason finales air.
 Before the Thanksgiving break, each of the three series will air their respective sixth episodes on November 17. NCIS Season 24 will lead the charge as always with "Ride or Die," which will take Torres deep undercover on a high-stakes mission in which he's forced to be the getaway driver for a kidnapper as dangerous as he is mysterious, played by True Blood alum James Frain . The agent will once again have to lean on his past work and play along to ensure everyone in the car makes it out alive in the end. Then, at 9 p.m., "My Companion" puts the New York team at the center of a sensitive case, where a Navy admiral sacrifices himself to save the life of an AI tech mogul who was the high-profile target of an assassination.

 Four action series. One of them is built around exactly the way you handle pressure,
 people, and a room that has just gone very quiet. Here is where you would survive the trilogy, and
 probably headline it. 
 here -->
 2014-2023 John Wick John Wick to Chapter 4 Reasonable to the line. Immovable past it. 
 You are precision with a grudge. You don't posture, you don't escalate, and you don't warn anybody twice. That is exactly why the people who know you are so careful never to be the reason you start. Why You Would Thrive Here 
 The Wick films run on discipline: an underworld with actual etiquette, a hero who honors
 every rule of it, and a world that unravels the instant someone breaks one against him.
 You share that quality. You are extraordinarily reasonable right up to the line, and then
 completely immovable past it.
 Focus, commitment and sheer will. You'd be the one carrying grief through three sequels
 and turning it into technique rather than noise.
 People wouldn't call you dangerous. They'd say your name quietly and let that do
 the work.
 The Code No Wasted Motion Say It Quietly 
 here -->
 2001-2023 Fast & Furious The Fast and the Furious to Fast X The mission can wait. The barbecue cannot. 
 You understand the thing the whole franchise is secretly about: the cars are spectacular, but the crew is the point. You collect people, you keep them, and you'd drive through a building for any one of them. Why You Would Thrive Here 
 This series went from street racing to orbit without ever changing its real subject, because
 loyalty scales and plot doesn't have to.
 You have the same instinct. You build a family out of whoever turns up, and then you defend
 it past the point of reason.
 You'd thrive here because the franchise rewards exactly your strengths: warmth, nerve,
 an absolute refusal to leave anyone behind, and a relaxed relationship with physics.
 The mission can wait. The barbecue cannot.

 1996-2025 Mission: Impossible Mission: Impossible to The Final Reckoning You have never once delegated the cliff. 
 You over-prepare and then take the dangerous part yourself anyway. It looks like control, but it's really responsibility. You have never worked out how to ask somebody else to carry the risk. Why You Would Thrive Here 
 This is the franchise of the plan that collapses on schedule: the team, the mask, the
 rooftop, and the one person sprinting flat out because sprinting is all that's left.
 You share that refusal to accept an outcome. Told the odds, you treat them as an
 administrative error.
 You'd thrive here because these films reward competence and loyalty in equal measure.
 The mission matters, but nobody on the team gets left on the wrong side of a door.
 Some people delegate the cliff. You have never once been that person.

 1988-2013 Die Hard Die Hard to A Good Day to Die Hard You declined to be the person who let it happen. 
 You are not the most trained person in the building, the best equipped, or the one anybody would have picked. You are simply the one still standing at the end, which turns out to be the only qualification that matters. Why You Would Thrive Here 
 Die Hard invented the modern action hero by making him mortal: outnumbered, out-planned,
 battered, and extremely funny about it.
 You share that stubbornness. Adversity doesn't make you noble, it makes you sarcastic,
 and then it makes you unstoppable.
 You'd thrive here because these films reward improvisation and nerve over preparation,
 and you've never had the luxury of preparing anyway.
 You didn't want any of this. You just declined to be the person who let it happen.

 'NCIS: Origins' Season 3 Is Welcoming Even More Familiar Faces
 Close Torres looking at John Smith in NCIS Season 24. Image via Sonja Flemming/CBS 
 Austin Stowell glancing off as Young Gibbs in NCIS: Origins Season 3, Episode 5. Image via CBS 
 Kyle Schmid placing his hand on Adam Campbell's shoulder in NCIS: Origins Season 3 Image via CBS 
 LL COOL J and Scott Caan walking together in NCIS: New York Image via CBS 
 Finally, Origins Season 3 will continue its streak of familiar NCIS guests in "Shot Through the Heart" at 10 p.m., bringing past and present together. In the present, Muse Watson will return from the flagship as the older Mike Franks, joining Gibbs as he seeks answers about what truly happened to Lala ( Mariel Molino ) years prior. Back in 1993, meanwhile, the team will scramble to find a mole after FBI Agent Casey Bloom ( Sean Harmon ) is shot, along the way highlighting the surprising bond growing between Lala and Franks ( Kyle Schmid ). Watson's appearance adds to what has been a season of reunions across the NCIS series, including Emily Wickersham , who will also appear once again as Ellie Bishop in the upcoming episode, Adam Campbell , Weatherly, and even a brief voice cameo by Rocky Carroll as the late Leon Vance.
 Aside from its Thanksgiving week break, the NCIS franchise will continue to air on Tuesdays on CBS throughout the rest of the fall television season. Stay tuned here at Collider for further updates on the procedural.
